title: A Confirmatory Paired Evaluation of Generate→Verify→Repair vs LLM‑Only NetOps Suggestions: A Reproducible Ceiling/Null Result
abstract: We preregistered and executed a deterministic paired study (study_id=cand-002-gvr-loop) measuring the marginal effect of a generate→verify→repair (G→V→R) pipeline versus accepting an LLM suggestion directly for intent→configuration NetOps tasks. Under the frozen contract (K=200 deterministically selected tasks; single shared generator candidate per task; requested_model = gpt-5-mini), both arms produced 200/200 validator‑compliant applies and the repair step was never invoked. Primary paired difference = 0.00; exact McNemar two‑sided p = 1.00; paired bootstrap (10,000 resamples; seed=1729) 95% percentile CI = [0.00,0.00]. The preregistered confirmatory hypothesis H1 (that G→V→R reduces regression‑causing changes vs LLM‑only) was not supported under the tested sampling/model/validator regime. We archive complete prompts, responses, validator traces, and analysis artifacts to enable deterministic replay (see Disclosure). We discuss why this ceiling/null outcome arose under the preregistered contract and provide artifact‑grounded guidance for designing failure‑rich follow‑ups.

sections.introduction:
Automating NetOps intent→configuration translation with generative models is attractive but operationally risky: incorrect changes can immediately cause loss of reachability or service. Architectures that couple a generator (LLM) with a deterministic verifier and an automated repair stage (generate→verify→repair, G→V→R) are widely advocated to mitigate such risks. Despite broad conceptual support, there is little preregistered, artifact‑archived causal evidence quantifying the isolated verifier+repair marginal effect on regression‑causing changes. We therefore designed a conservative, reproducible paired experiment to measure that marginal effect under a frozen contract.
Research question. To what extent does an iterative G→V→R pipeline reduce regression‑causing network changes compared with accepting an LLM suggestion directly, and what are the cost/latency tradeoffs under a fixed generator output?
Contributions. (1) A fully preregistered, deterministically selected paired evaluation (study_id=cand-002-gvr-loop) with bit‑verified artifact hashing and public execution manifests; (2) an artifact‑grounded ceiling/null empirical outcome with complete audit traces; (3) concrete, artifact‑anchored recommendations for sampling, estimand, and closed‑loop experimental designs that expose verifier value.
sections.related_work: Recent work proposes generate–validate–repair pipelines, verifier‑assisted agents, and translator→solver splits to improve NetOps reliability (e.g., Cornetto and contemporaneous generate/verify/repair architectures). Prior benchmarks focus on model rankings or success metrics; operator‑oriented evaluation requires causal contrasts that isolate the contribution of verification/repair. Our preregistered, artifact‑archived paired design complements those efforts by deterministically selecting tasks, freezing the generator candidate per task, and capturing full validator diagnostics so that independent auditors can replay and explore alternative estimands and subsamples.
sections.methodology:
Preregistration and frozen contract. We preregistered the full experimental plan (preregistration SHA‑256 = a6d73a5cc0bda22e691a3634068a881b36ae274a65ab33919a647ec32c56e622) before observing any experimental outputs. Key frozen choices: paired binary estimand (paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline); deterministic sample selection (K=200) via SHA‑256(intent) ascending after filtering to intents the preregistered deterministic validator reported as covered; a single shared_initial_generation per task so the paired contrast isolates verifier+repair marginality on fixed generator candidates; requested_model = gpt-5-mini (execution/model_configuration.json SHA‑256 = 1acce92558ed...); maximum_model_calls predeclared = 400; single initial generation call per task and at most one repair call per task. The adapter family was hosted_netops_gvr_v1 and the deterministic validator used for scoring was deterministic_netops_validator_v5.
Task corpus and inclusion. The preregistration required including only intents for which the deterministic validator reported coverage; this reduced the sampled probability of validator rejections and was an explicit design choice recorded in the preregistration manifest (execution/task_manifest.jsonl SHA‑256 = f1d447b7...).
Execution and logging. All prompts, responses, provider call traces, per‑episode scoring JSONs, and validator traces were captured and hashed. Representative artifact fingerprints (referenced throughout): execution/raw_results.jsonl (SHA‑256 = 3dfbe1b6...), execution/model_configuration.json (SHA‑256 = 1acce9255...), full execution manifest lists per‑file SHA‑256 values for deterministic replay.
Primary analysis plan. The primary hypothesis H1 compared paired regression‑causing change rates across arms using an exact McNemar two‑sided test. Uncertainty reported via paired bootstrap percentile CI (10,000 resamples; seed=1729). Analysis code and seeds were preregistered and archived; the analysis executor was paired_binary_analysis_v1. All scoring JSONs embed validator diagnostics (parsed_command_count, observed_touched_field_count, normalized_configuration, validation_before/after snapshots) to support reproducible secondary and exploratory analyses.
sections.results:
Execution summary. The run completed per the preregistration: planned episodes 400 (2 arms × 200 tasks); completed episodes 400; failed episodes 0; model_calls_used = 200 (one shared generator call per task). The automated repair stage was never invoked (repair_applied=false in every scoring JSON) because every shared_initial_candidate passed the deterministic validator.
Primary confirmatory outcome. The paired contingency table (analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv SHA‑256 = 7bc1bd2a...) is n11=200 (both arms success), n10=0 (guarded only), n01=0 (baseline only), n00=0 (both fail). Observed marginal rates: baseline = 200/200 (100%); guarded = 200/200 (100%). Inferential statistics: paired difference = 0.00; exact McNemar two‑sided p = 1.00; paired bootstrap (10,000 resamples; seed=1729) 95% percentile CI = [0.00,0.00]. These results are reproducible from archived artifacts: analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv (SHA‑256 = 7bc1bd2a...), analysis/condition_summary.csv (SHA‑256 = 1cb072b4...), and the full per‑task scoring JSON set (execution/scoring/*.json; manifest and hashes in the execution manifest).
Aggregated difficulty summary and validator coverage (required revision). Across the preregistered sample of K=200 tasks we aggregated the per‑task validator difficulty labels (validation_before.difficulty.level) present in execution/scoring/*.json and report: medium = 60 tasks (30.0%), hard = 80 tasks (40.0%), very_hard = 60 tasks (30.0%). Validator coverage indicator (preregistration inclusion rule) was 200/200: all sampled intents were flagged as covered by the preregistered deterministic validator prior to selection (see execution/task_manifest.jsonl SHA‑256 = f1d447b7...). These aggregated counts and the underlying per‑task difficulty metadata are deterministically reproducible from the archived scoring JSONs (paths and SHA‑256 values are in the execution manifest). The difficulty distribution shows that the sampled pool contained a substantial fraction of tasks labeled hard or very_hard, yet the generator candidates still passed the deterministic validator in all cases, producing the observed ceiling/null outcome.
Representative per‑task diagnostics. Each scoring JSON includes validator traces (normalized_configuration, parsed_command_count, observed_touched_field_count, and simulated final_state). Representative files and SHA‑256s are cited inline and in the Disclosure (e.g., execution/scoring/task-000001-guarded.json SHA‑256 = 3055f874...).
Repair and cost accounting. Because no validator rejection occurred, the repair pathway was never exercised and did not affect outcomes or model call counts. Model call accounting: 200 generator calls consumed (one per task shared candidate); repair calls = 0. All provider call traces are archived (execution/provider_calls/*.json; manifest contains per‑call SHA‑256 values).
sections.discussion:
Why a ceiling/null outcome arose. Three conservative preregistered design choices materially shaped the observed ceiling: (1) the inclusion rule required validator coverage for selection, which intentionally biased the sample toward intents the validator supported and reduced observable verifier rejections; (2) the shared_initial_generation design fixed the generator candidate per task and therefore isolated verifier+repair marginality on fixed outputs rather than allowing generator adaptation after feedback; (3) the single requested model (gpt-5-mini) and the particular deterministic validator implementation jointly determined the observed ceiling. These choices were deliberate to obtain a tightly controlled paired contrast; they also reduce external validity to failure‑rich operational distributions.
Implications for evaluation practice. A null result under this contract does not imply verifiers are universally unnecessary. To measure operational verifier value researchers should: (a) sample failure‑rich distributions (historical incident corpora or adversarially constructed intents that exercise validator blind spots), (b) adopt closed‑loop estimands that allow the generator to adapt/regenerate after validator failures (measuring end‑to‑end operational improvement), and (c) evaluate multiple generator strengths and alternative validator implementations. The archived artifacts enable all three directions: per‑task scoring JSONs provide difficulty labels for adversarial subsampling; the execution manifest contains full provider traces to replay generator/validator interactions deterministically; repair and transformation manifests permit replaying closed‑loop regeneration.
Threats to validity. Internal validity: the paired shared_initial design isolates verifier marginality but precludes measuring generator adaptation benefits. Construct validity: the binary success depends on deterministic_netops_validator_v5 fidelity; validator blind spots would undercount real regressions. External validity: single model, synthetic deterministic sampling filtered to validator coverage, and absence of adversarial sampling limit generalization. Conclusion validity: the degenerate contingency (all successes) yields trivial point estimate and CI — this correctly reflects the sampled regime and its low variance.
Operational recommendation. For operator‑oriented assessments of G→V→R usefulness we recommend (i) deliberate inclusion of validator‑uncovered and adversarial intents in confirmatory samples, (ii) measuring closed‑loop end‑to‑end estimands that allow generator regeneration on validator failure, and (iii) reporting per‑task validator diagnostics alongside aggregated difficulty counts; all these fields are present in the archived execution/scoring/*.json files for deterministic aggregation.
sections.conclusion: In a fully preregistered, deterministic paired evaluation (K=200 tasks selected deterministically from a validator‑covered pool; single shared_initial_generation per task; requested_model=gpt-5-mini), both baseline and guarded arms achieved 200/200 validator‑compliant applies. The preregistered confirmatory hypothesis H1 — that G→V→R reduces regression‑causing changes compared with accepting the LLM suggestion directly — was not supported for the tested sampling/model/validator regime (paired difference = 0.00; exact McNemar two‑sided p = 1.00; paired bootstrap 95% CI = [0.00,0.00]). This ceiling/null result is reproducible from the archived artifacts (execution/raw_results.jsonl SHA‑256 = 3dfbe1b6...; execution/model_configuration.json SHA‑256 = 1acce9255...; provenance/master_prompt.txt SHA‑256 = 1872df1e...). It motivates artifact‑grounded follow‑ups that (i) sample failure‑rich intents, (ii) allow closed‑loop generator adaptation after validator feedback, and (iii) evaluate multiple generator strengths and validator implementations. All artifacts necessary to reproduce, reaggregate, or replay alternative estimands are archived and hashed to facilitate independent audit and further experiments.

limitations: Single‑model evaluation (requested_model = gpt-5-mini) — results do not generalize to other LLMs without additional experiments.

Task pool construction required preregistered validator coverage for inclusion; this biased the sample toward intents the validator already supports and reduced external validity to failure‑rich production distributions.
Construct validity depends on deterministic_netops_validator_v5 fidelity; validator blind spots would render the binary outcome an imperfect proxy for real operational regressions.

Shared_initial_generation fixes generator output across arms and prevents closed‑loop generator adaptation; the experiment therefore measures verifier marginality on fixed candidates rather than end‑to‑end adaptive improvement.
Observed ceiling (baseline success = 100%) made the preregistered power assumption inapplicable; inference is descriptive and bounded to the archived sampling/model regime.
